Treatment regimens are primarily based on FDCs, but in certain cases, single-component products may also need to be administered. 3. The recommended doses are designed for once-daily regimens and aim to avoid the need for splitting tablets whenever feasible. 4. The doses are generally set below the upper limit of the therapeutic range to reduce the risk of toxicity. These guidelines replace the interim recommendations published by WHO in 2009, which provided dosing instructions for the use of available FDC TB medicines in children. Once children reach a body weight of 25 kilograms, adult dosage recommendations can be followed, and adult formulations of the medications can be used.
